question.prompt: A flower bouquet contains pink roses, red roses, pink carnations, and red carnations. One third of the pink flowers are roses, three fourths of the red flowers are carnations, and six tenths of the flowers are pink. What percent of the flowers are carnations?

solutions.explanation:
Find the fraction of all flowers that are carnations in each color group. Since \(\frac13\) of the pink flowers are roses, the remaining \(\frac23\) are carnations. Pink flowers make up \(\frac6{10}=\frac35\) of the bouquet, so pink carnations make up
\[
\frac35\cdot\frac23=\frac25
\]
of all flowers.

The remaining \(\frac25\) of the flowers are red. Since \(\frac34\) of those are carnations, red carnations make up
\[
\frac25\cdot\frac34=\frac3{10}
\]
of all flowers. Every carnation is either pink or red, and these groups do not overlap. Therefore the fraction of carnations is
\[
\frac25+\frac3{10}
=\frac4{10}+\frac3{10}
=\frac7{10}=70\%.
\]
The answer is \(70\%\), choice \(\mathrm{E}\).
solutions.title: Combine the two color groups
